melanesia.name: Melanesia
melanesia.remarks: The western arc of Pacific islands, and the part of Oceania that reaches into the Coral Triangle.

micronesia.name: Micronesia
micronesia.remarks: Thousands of small islands north of the equator, mostly atolls, with a good deal of the Second World War still on the seabed between them.

polynesia.name: Polynesia
polynesia.remarks: A triangle of islands covering more area than any continent, settled by people navigating with stars, swell and birds.

tasman_sea.name: Tasman Sea
tasman_sea.remarks: Rough often enough to have earned its nickname. Cold water, and great whites at the southern end.

solomon_sea.name: Solomon Sea
solomon_sea.remarks: Deep trenches close inshore, and wrecks from the 1942 fighting in water shallow enough to dive.

bismarck_sea.name: Bismarck Sea
bismarck_sea.remarks: Volcanic, with hydrothermal vents on the seabed and reef immediately above them.

great_barrier_reef.name: Great Barrier Reef
great_barrier_reef.remarks: The largest structure built by living things anywhere, running two thousand three hundred kilometres and made of about three thousand separate reefs. Nobody dives all of it.

ningaloo_reef.name: Ningaloo Reef
ningaloo_reef.remarks: A fringing reef on the western side where whale sharks arrive every autumn, close enough to shore to swim out to.

australia.name: Australia
australia.remarks: Reef along the north, kelp and great whites along the south, and a coastline long enough that the two have almost nothing in common.

new_zealand.name: New Zealand
new_zealand.remarks: Cold, clear and volcanic, with kelp where the tropics would put coral. A warm current reaches the Poor Knights and carries subtropical species much further south than they ought to manage.

papua_new_guinea.name: Papua New Guinea
papua_new_guinea.remarks: Inside the Coral Triangle, with reef, muck diving, and a very large number of ships and aircraft lost here in the 1940s.

fiji.name: Fiji
fiji.remarks: Straddles the antimeridian, so its east edge is numerically west of its west one. Known for soft coral, and a great deal of it.

solomon_islands.name: Solomon Islands
solomon_islands.remarks: Nearly a thousand islands. The water off Guadalcanal is called Iron Bottom Sound, and the reason becomes obvious underwater.

vanuatu.name: Vanuatu
vanuatu.remarks: Volcanic and seismically busy. A troopship sunk in 1942 lies close enough to the beach to be dived by walking in.

new_caledonia.name: New Caledonia
new_caledonia.remarks: Ringed by the second largest barrier reef in the world, enclosing one of the largest lagoons.

palau.name: Palau
palau.remarks: Small, and wildly out of proportion to its size underwater. It declared the first shark sanctuary in the world, and has a landlocked lake full of jellyfish that lost their sting for want of anything to sting.

federated_states_of_micronesia.name: Federated States of Micronesia
federated_states_of_micronesia.remarks: Chuuk Lagoon holds a Japanese fleet sunk at anchor in 1944 — dozens of ships in divable depths, cargo still in the holds.

marshall_islands.name: Marshall Islands
marshall_islands.remarks: Twenty-nine atolls, including Bikini, where nuclear testing sank a fleet in a lagoon that people now dive on purpose.

kiribati.name: Kiribati
kiribati.remarks: Spread across the equator and the antimeridian at once, which makes it the only country in all four hemispheres.

nauru.name: Nauru
nauru.remarks: Twenty-one square kilometres, the third smallest country in the world, with a reef edge that drops away almost immediately.

tuvalu.name: Tuvalu
tuvalu.remarks: Nine low atolls with a highest point around four and a half metres, and a very direct interest in what the sea level does next.

tonga.name: Tonga
tonga.remarks: Humpbacks arrive every winter to calve, and this is one of very few places where swimming with them is allowed.

samoa.name: Samoa
samoa.remarks: Volcanic, reef-fringed, with a trench dropping away to the north.

french_polynesia.name: French Polynesia
french_polynesia.remarks: A hundred and eighteen islands scattered over an area the size of Europe. The passes between lagoon and ocean run hard with the tide, and grey reef sharks stack up in them by the hundred.

cook_islands.name: Cook Islands
cook_islands.remarks: Fifteen islands in two widely separated groups, with clear water and very little traffic in it.

niue.name: Niue
niue.remarks: A single raised coral island with no rivers, so nothing silts the water. The visibility is reliably among the best anywhere.

guam.name: Guam
guam.remarks: A German ship sunk in 1914 and a Japanese one sunk in 1944 lie touching each other in the harbour, which nobody planned.

northern_mariana_islands.name: Northern Mariana Islands
northern_mariana_islands.remarks: The Mariana Trench runs alongside, making this the nearest inhabited land to the deepest point on the planet.

wallis_and_futuna.name: Wallis and Futuna
wallis_and_futuna.remarks: Two small island groups, a lagoon around one of them, and very few visitors to either.

tokelau.name: Tokelau
tokelau.remarks: Three atolls, no airport, and a highest point of about five metres.

american_samoa.name: American Samoa
american_samoa.remarks: Volcanic islands with a deep natural harbour, and a national park that includes the reef around it.
